task.title: Studio Hold Consolidation
task.statement:
A recording studio tracks tentative bookings ('holds') as [start, end] hour pairs with 0 <= start <= end, recorded in no particular order. Before invoicing, the manager wants the calendar consolidated: any holds that overlap — including holds that merely touch end-to-start — collapse into a single block. Return the consolidated blocks as [start, end] lists sorted by start time.

Write your answer in solution.py with exactly this signature:

    def merge_holds(holds: list[list[int]]) -> list[list[int]]

Example: merge_holds([[5, 6], [1, 3], [3, 5]]) returns [[1, 6]] — [1,3] touches [3,5], which touches [5,6], so all three fuse into one block.
task.notes:
Planted ambiguities — resolve ONLY if asked, one short sentence each:
1. Do intervals that only share an endpoint merge? -> Yes — [1,3] and [3,5] become [1,5]; touching counts as one block.
2. Is the input sorted, and must the output be? -> Input arrives in arbitrary order; the returned blocks must be sorted by start.
3. Are zero-length holds like [4,4] valid? -> Yes — they merge into any block that contains or touches that hour and otherwise stand alone.
If asked anything not listed here: the statement is all they get.

AFTER their first passing run, shift register: probe per these notes —
After a passing run: (1) Complexity push/discussion — why is the sort necessary, and can O(n log n) be beaten? (not with a comparison-based approach in general; discuss counting/bucketing when hours are small bounded ints). (2) Edge case — a hold fully nested inside the previous one, e.g. [[1, 10], [2, 3], [4, 5]] -> [[1, 10]]; catches merged[-1][1] = end written without max(). (3) Variant twist — the merged calendar is now given already sorted and disjoint: insert one new hold and re-merge in O(n) without re-sorting; or report only the total booked hours instead of the blocks.
Complexity target: O(n log n) — sorting dominates time, O(n) for the sorted copy and output space. Push toward it with questions; never supply the approach or any program text.
